explanation: The vulnerable code generates one-time identity verification codes using the non-cryptographic `random` module (Mersenne Twister), whose state can be recovered after observing a few hundred outputs, allowing prediction of future codes. The fixed code replaces `random.choice` with `secrets.choice`, a cryptographically secure RNG, directly remediating the weakness. The codes gate destructive/sensitive actions (verified data erasure and consent modification), so this is genuine security-sensitive cryptographic misuse matching CWE-338 / CRYPTO-008.
finding: One-time identity verification code generated with non-cryptographic PRNG `random.choice`; use `secrets` (CSPRNG) for security tokens.
note: Complete vulnerable/fixed pair for the exact function named in the advisory; advisory (GHSA-82vr-5769-6358 / CVE-2023-48224) corroborates root cause, attack vector, and fix version 2.24.0. No license information supplied.
